I've been farming this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou well — the soil here on the North China Plain is decent but the groundwater has been dropping every year since I was young. My main system is wheat-maize on most of my land. That rotation is what I know, what the market rewards, and what the county extension has pushed for decades. My two kids help some weekends but mostly work in the city, so I can't take on too much cotton — it's too labor-heavy to manage alone at my age. I'll keep a modest cotton plot because the price has been reasonable these past two years, but I won't expand it. Millet I grow on my lower-quality sandy plots — it needs less water, less fertilizer, and I can sell it locally for decent money as a specialty grain.

For wheat, I'll plant the county-recommended improved variety. I put down base fertilizer before planting and topdress at jointing. I irrigate at overwintering, jointing, and heading — three times, maybe four if it stays dry in May. I've cut back on a fourth irrigation compared to when I was younger because the well costs keep rising.

For summer maize, I direct-seed hybrid seed right after wheat harvest using rotary tillage. No time to plough — I need the maize in the ground fast to catch the season. Two or three irrigations, heavy nitrogen at tasseling.

Cotton goes on about 25 mu of separate plots. I plough those in spring, use hybrid seed, and spray more frequently — bollworm and aphids are always a problem. But I know what I'm doing after 40 years.

Millet on the remaining 14 mu. Simple management, not much irrigation needed.
